Definition: from G2596 and G3572; to pierce thoroughly, i.e. (figuratively) to agitate violently ("sting to the quick"):--prick.
BiblicalUsage: When they heard this, they were pricked in their heart, and said to Peter and the rest of the apostles, Men and brethren, what shall we do.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the prick of the heart is the beginning of repentance, and it is the Spirit's work, not the preacher's.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
